subject: Proposal: dedicated reservation sizing & ramp choices — Crestline Therapeutics
messages:
From: Adam Levine <adam@crestlinetherapeutics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Hernandez <sofia.hernandez@crestlinetherapeutics.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — initial metrics attached

Hi Ben / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're at the point of sizing the dedicated footprint for our inference pipelines and want a proposal that maps to our expected ramp. High level:

- Initial inference footprint: steady-state ~24 A100-equivalent GPUs (mixed T4 for non-latency work today)
- Peak forecast: ~96 GPUs during production ramp (models 1.5–2.0B tokens/day)
- Desired ramp window: up to ~8–12 weeks from pilot to peak
- Must have geo redundancy (us-east and us-west) for failover and data residency needs
- Interested in warm-start credits / burst windows for early traffic spikes

Can you send 2–3 reservation options that vary by minimum GPU floor, ramp cadence, and failure-runbook (how we handle regional capacity constraints)? Also include: activation lead time, minimum contract term, and any trial/pilot mechanics (e.g., 2-week pilot with convert-to-reservation).

I attached a small export of our request rates and seq-length distribution. Happy to hop on a short call to align.

Attachment: Current_workload_metrics.csv (csv)

Regards,
Adam Levine
Head of ML Infrastructure
Crestline Therapeutics
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Adam Levine <adam@crestlinetherapeutics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sofia Hernandez <sofia.hernandez@crestlinetherapeutics.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — initial metrics attached

Adam — thanks for the clear brief and the metric export. Per your ask, attached is a concise options sheet and a quick run-of-play for onboarding. High level options (summarized):

1) Pilot Lane (low friction)
- Min GPUs: 8 (single-region; us-west)
- Ramp: 2–4 weeks to ~32 GPUs with predictable burst credits
- Best for validating model performance and SLOs; converts to a dedicated reservation with no dry-run fee

2) Progressive Standard (recommended for your forecast)
- Min GPUs: 24 (primary region us-west)
- Target peak: 96 (geo-burst allowed to us-east)
- Ramp: staged over 8–12 weeks; weekly activation windows (2–4 GPU increments typical)
- Warm-start credits: 100 GPU-hours during months 1–2 to smooth activation burn

3) Anchored Geo-Redundant (aggressive SLO)
- Min GPUs: 48 (split 60/40 across two regions)
- Target peak: 96 with pre-provisioned failover lanes
- Ramp: 6–10 weeks with guaranteed warm-standby capacity and SLA uplift

Operational notes included in the attachment:
- Minimum contract term: 3 months for Pilot convert; 12 months for Standard/Anchored pricing tiers
- Activation lead time: 3–5 business days for Pilot; 7–14 days for Standard/Anchored depending on GPU class and region
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to compatible model variants and cross-region burst if primary capacity constrained (we define compatibility matrix and token impact during onboarding)

Next steps: if you prefer the Progressive Standard, we can draft an SOW + mutual action plan and provision a 2-week pilot (8 GPUs) to run acceptance tests (latency p95, throughput, and cost per token). I attached the options PDF and a quick cost delta chart.

Attachment: Crestline_Dedicated_Options_v1.pdf (pdf)

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Adam Levine <adam@crestlinetherapeutics.com>
Cc: Sofia Hernandez <sofia.hernandez@crestlinetherapeutics.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — initial metrics attached

Quick technical notes from our infra side to make sure the proposal aligns with Crestline's workload:

- Sequence length & kernels: Your distribution looks ~80% <1024 tokens; that favors continuous batching with optimized attention kernels. We'll use tiled-kernel selection for longer requests to maximize throughput.
- KV cache sizing: For a 96-GPU peak, plan for ~1.6–2.2 TB of aggregate KV store (depends on model variants). We'll provide a sizing worksheet in the onboarding doc.
- Quantization path: Recommend starting with a q4_0 profile for the standard lane to cut token cost ~30% without a large quality delta. We'll run an eval on the pilot set to validate.
- Warm-start mechanics: Warm-standby = reserved lanes preloaded with model weights but throttled until you need them; warm-start credits will be consumed on activation.

Proposed technical validation for the pilot (2 weeks):
- Smoke: 48-hour latency sweep (p50/p95)
- Load: 72-hour sustained throughput run to 2x projected peak
- Quality: prompt-set regression test against a holdout set

If Adam is aligned to the Progressive Standard, we should carve out a 2-week pilot window and schedule an infra runbook review. Happy to join the call next week.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Adam Levine <adam@crestlinetherapeutics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Hernandez <sofia.hernandez@crestlinetherapeutics.com>, procurement@crestlinetherapeutics.com
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — initial metrics attached

Ben / Karthik — thanks for the options and the technical notes. We're inclined to move forward with the Progressive Standard option, subject to two clarifications before procurement issues a PO:

1) Minimum activation footprint for month 1: please confirm if we are expected to maintain 24 GPUs at day 1 of the reservation, or if the Pilot-convert path allows an initial lower floor (we'd like to start at 16 GPUs in week 1 and step to 24 in week 2).
2) Doc signing / SOW flow: send us the SOW outline and a DocuSign link so procurement can start the legal review and PO routing.

If you can confirm the activation flexibility in writing and share the SOW, we'll route for approval this week. Attaching a light SOW outline to speed review.

Attachment: SOW_outline.docx (docx)

Best,
Adam Levine
Head of ML Infrastructure
Crestline Therapeutics
procurement@crestlinetherapeutics.com
